changed_in.5.2: A write that went through now hands back the file it was called on, so one write can be written straight onto the end of another — `writing:write("cocoa"):write(",")`. Earlier versions hand back `true` instead, which says the write went through and nothing more; a chain written against them stops at the first `:` with an attempt to index a boolean.
changed_in.5.3: How a number is written changed when whole numbers became a kind of number in their own right. A whole number is now written out in full through the integer format, where before every number went through the float format — fourteen significant digits, and exponent notation once a value needed more than that, so a large whole number reached the file as something like `1e+15` rather than as its digits. A number with a fractional part is unaffected.
changed_in.5.5: Two changes. A write that did not get through now hands back a fourth value after the usual three: how many bytes the call did get out before it stopped, counted across all of its arguments together. And a number is now written exactly as `tostring()` renders it, so a whole-valued float keeps its trailing `.0` and a fractional one is written with enough digits to read back as the same number; earlier versions write a whole-valued float with no fractional part at all, which makes the file disagree with what `tostring()` on the same value would have produced.
